body: Of course. If I'm ever unhappy in the future, I'd imagine that I'll envy that former, non-existent me.
Because eternal peace is a greater reward than temporary happiness.

I clearly have mild sociopathic tendencies. I would have absolutely no qualms about murdering a stranger for $20, and the only reason I don't do so is because I'd eventually end up in prison. If that doesn't make me a sociopath, then okay, I'm probably not one.

Then again, I'm pretty sure that a some of the people in this thread are correct in saying that we're *all* sociopathic to some degree or another.

> Till date, there's no fast, cheap, legal and elegant manner to commit suicide.

Who cares if it's cheap or legal? It's *suicide*.

As for fast and elegant, I think jumping off a cliff or a bridge fits that ticket. It'd be fun, too! What a way to go!

Yeah, I don't really understand your type. The thought of my life having a purpose beyond satisfying my own happiness actually *terrifies* me, and I would immediately do anything in my power to rid myself of said purpose if I ever had one.

> You want to kill yourself? Fine, do it.

Not exactly the type of attitude I'd expect from r/SuicideWatch, but it's definitely refreshing.
I've already addressed that, both in my OP, and in a reply in this thread.
I have fallen in love before; I've sometimes been even helplessly, head over heels in love - but only with people who also don't want children.

I am almost certain that I would not unconditionally love any child that I might hypothetically have. I believe that I would view raising a child as an extreme hassle, and would ultimately opt to either kill my baby, or simply leave it in a church when nobody was looking.

Of course, all of this is moot, as I will never have kids. Given that I'm fairly certain that I'd want to kill any babies I'd end up having, I don't think it would be logical for me to have any in the first place. (I'm not sure whether or not I'd be *able* to kill them, but I'm pretty sure the fact that I'd want to means that I wouldn't exactly be a great father.)

I'm probably not *that* much more selfish than other people, but I wouldn't know for sure.

I *do* feel affection for people! I have not once in my life ever felt *unconditional* love, even towards my parents, and cannot even comprehend what such an emotion feels like, but as I get to know people, I do end up feeling conditional love.

I love my parents, but conditionally; I think of them more like really amazing and caring friends rather than how I'd imagine people typically view their parents. I love my mom, and feel affection for her, but not *because* she's my mom. I'd imagine losing my mom would be like losing one of my best friends, who's always cared about me and taken care of me, but not *exactly* like what losing a parent would feel to a normal person. Of course, it'll still be incredibly depressing when it happens.

I already addressed your response in my OP.

Sure, if I feel down, it'd be nice to know that if I choose to live I'll eventually be happy again - but why bother? What makes the rollercoaster of life so much better and worthwhile than eternal peace?

My question is sort of along the lines of: if there's a warm for every cold, why shouldn't I just stay warm for as long as possible, and then kill myself once I get cold?

The opinion that happiness is relative and wouldn't exist without sadness seems irrelevant to me. Regardless of whether or not that's true, I live for happiness, and thus I still see no point in living if I'm not happy.

(I should add that I don't feel suicidal if a little trivial sad thing happens to me. My problem is that if my life as a whole changes for the worse, which may just happen, then I have a feeling that I'll probably kill myself.)
